policy_passages.html: You can claim back 25p every time an individual donates £1 to your charity or community amateur sports club (CASC). This is called Gift Aid.
You must be recognised as a charity or CASC for tax purposes.
• have paid at least as much in Income Tax or Capital Gains Tax in that tax year as you want to claim in Gift Aid
• make a Gift Aid declaration that gives you permission to claim it
You can claim Gift Aid on donations from individuals. The donor must:
• have paid the same amount or more in Income Tax or Capital Gains Tax in that tax year
• that are a payment for goods or services or made because your charity or CASC bought goods and services
• where the donor gets a ‘benefit’ over a certain limit
• from charity cards or of vouchers, for example Charities Aid Foundation (CAF) vouchers

decision_question: Can the specified receipt be included in the charity’s ordinary Gift Aid claim under the supplied policy?
customer_scenario:
I run a small, independent charity which attempts to help people struggling with their vet costs. I have several people who pay monthly by direct debit and also receive some one off donations.

Additional customer information:
Robyn Ellis paid the charity £260 on 4 February 2026. The bookkeeping sheet calls it a donation, but January emails show she accepted a £260 price for advertising her grooming salon in the charity's newsletter and on its website. The booking was confirmed after her payment, and the advertisement appeared as agreed. Her separate £20 cash gift in December was unrelated. The charity has an HMRC recognition letter, but Robyn's tax position and any Gift Aid declaration for the £260 have not been checked.
